panels.visual: The grumpy tortoise on the south slope of the Acropolis lifting a bored eyebrow at us
panels.caption: Meet the tortoise. It has heard a story or two.

panels.visual: Aeschylus (bald old tragedian in a robe, writing) in Sicily in the sun, a scroll on his knee
panels.caption: Aeschylus, the first great writer of tragedies, died in Sicily around 456 BC.

panels.visual: A giant eagle carrying a tortoise high above a rocky Sicilian hillside, below a bald man sitting, the sun glinting off his head
panels.caption: The story goes that an eagle mistook the old man's bald head for a rock and dropped the tortoise.

panels.visual: The tortoise close-up with a deadpan face, one eyebrow raised, and a tiny sign reading 'story, not report'
panels.caption: A bald playwright, though? Almost certainly made up.
